client_transport: strangertest.handle.TasksHTTPTransport (HTTPTransport modern=True + Mcp-Name=taskId on tasks/*), MCP 2026-07-28, tasks extension declared in _meta clientCapabilities
gateway_config_run:
# TASK-HANDLE gate: agentgateway in front of the practice task server, with
# PER-USER upstream identity. Ports are double-brace placeholders; the driver
# (integration/handle_gateway_gate.py) writes a port-substituted copy to a
# scratch dir and refuses to run with any placeholder left, or with a port
# outside its block. Everything is loopback-only: agentgateway binds all
# interfaces by default, so every listener is pinned to 127.0.0.1 and stats /
# readiness are off.
#   client --(user JWT)--> agentgateway 4230  (jwtAuth: local AS JWKS)
#   agentgateway --(the same validated user JWT, backendAuth.passthrough)-->
#     practice task server 4280/mcp
# The practice server identifies the caller by its Authorization header, so
# users A and B stay distinct at the upstream, which does the task owner check.
config:
  adminAddr: 127.0.0.1:4231
  statsAddr: "off"
  readinessAddr: "off"
gateways:
  handle:
    port: 4230
    bindAddress: 127.0.0.1
routes:
- name: handle-mcp
  gateways: handle
  policies:
    jwtAuth:
      mode: strict
      providers:
      - issuer: https://local-as.test
        audiences: [agentgateway-api]
        jwks:
          url: http://127.0.0.1:4290/jwks
  backends:
  - mcp:
      statefulMode: stateful
      targets:
      - name: tasks
        mcp:
          host: http://127.0.0.1:4280/mcp
        policies:
          backendAuth:
            passthrough: {}
upstream_auth: per-user: backendAuth.passthrough forwards the validated user JWT
source_evidence: agentgateway v1.7.0 crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/session.rs:736-756: GetTask/UpdateTask/CancelTask requests are parsed, authorized only by the configured static mcpAuthorization policy (authorize_task_request, session.rs:256-280: ResourceType::Task(target, taskId) against CEL rules), then sent to the upstream (send_single). No binding of a taskId to the user who created it.
handler.rs:205-237: taskIds in CreateTaskResult/GetTaskResult are rewritten to '<target>+<id>' only when there is no default target (multiplexing); with one target they pass through unchanged.
streamablehttp.rs:428-441: tasks/* are name-bearing; the Mcp-Name header must equal params.taskId, else -32020 'invalid MCP routing header'.
